turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: After the October rains, 18 tonnes of waste and over 350 tyres washed up on El Médano beach.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Mm. Straight into the sea. [pause]

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Meganoticias says altered stream beds funneled everything down. The federal office also pulled 12.5 tonnes of debris from San José beaches.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Really? I keep picturing those stream beds like old desert roads.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Meanwhile over in Mulegé they spent 713 million pesos on works including a new aqueduct.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: And federal funding there fell 70 percent.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Meanwhile the city just spent 302.9 million pesos on water lines and leaks.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Gringo Gazette reports the D1 plant now pushes 130 litres per second after OOMSAPAS took over.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: They also added 20 free water trucks and repaired 4,312 leaks.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: And D2 is three quarters done, set to add 250 litres per second once finished.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Los Cabos also found 25 illegal connections this year.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Senator Zatarain wants up to ten years in prison for theft.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: This is Radio BCS2050.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Today we ask one question.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: When the desert sends water and waste the same way, where does the city put its trust? [chuckle]

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Gringo Gazette reports that Los Cabos invested 302.9 million pesos in water and sanitation ahead of the mayor's second report.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: They repaired over 4,312 leaks and installed 39,058 new meters.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Plus 20 free water trucks for people who still need them.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: After ending the private contract, they spent 78 million pesos on the D1 plant.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: It now runs at 130 liters per second instead of 70.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The mayor is set to deliver her second report on 21 November, right after these investments.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Along with those mains they also put in fifteen kilometres of new sewers for better drainage.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: What does that change feel like for families who used to wait on trucks?

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: I keep thinking about the quiet mornings when the truck finally arrives.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The D2 plant in Cabo San Lucas sits at 76.58% built.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: One point seven eight billion pesos so far, adding 250 liters per second once finished.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The city is looking for more support to expand capacity even beyond the current plans.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: I keep picturing the long road south and how water shapes every stop along it.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: They want another two point one billion from the federal government to push D1 further.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: To reach 200 liters per second there.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: La Sonoreña 2 already has 708 million pesos approved.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Meanwhile Meganoticias says the thirtieth of October rains sent eighteen tonnes of waste onto El Médano beach.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Over 350 tyres came with it.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Another twelve point five tonnes landed on San José beaches, along with fifteen vehicles.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: It makes me wonder how the waves sound when they carry all that debris onto the sand.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The Pacific light hits differently after a storm like that one on 30 October.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Specialists point to altered stream beds that now funnel everything straight to the sea.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The engineers' association wants all three government levels to fund proper storm drainage.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: A sewage spill that has sat unfixed for more than 20 days is now eating into the Transpeninsular highway.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The SCT office in BCS confirmed damage mainly on the shoulders between San José and Cabo San Lucas. [pause]

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: How long before a full assessment also looks at the sanitary drainage underneath?

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Mm. The rain and the road feel connected in ways we rarely see until they break.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Over in Mulegé, Tribuna de México says the mayor reported 713 million pesos in public works across five years.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: More than 215 million of that went to water works, including 23 kilometres of new mains.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: 240 million pesos of the total went specifically to work in Guerrero Negro alone.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The desert light changes when water arrives after so many dry seasons. [laugh]

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: They just began the first seven kilometres of the Palo Verde to Santa Rosalía aqueduct with Conagua.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Federal works funding dropped 70% this year.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Still, over 150,000 visitors come each season to Bahía Concepción. [chuckle]

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What would you ask the engineers who keep the pipes and the highway from meeting like this?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: I would ask how the desert itself might guide the next stretch of pipe.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: East Cape sits at the edge of growth, with that reef ecology pulling at one side and the ANP limits holding the other.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Mm. What does daily life feel like there when the water supply is already thin before any new hotel arrives?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Gringo Gazette reports Los Cabos just spent 302.9 million pesos on water and sanitation upgrades.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: One number, yet it reaches right into those coastal towns.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: They raised the D1 plant from 70 to 130 liters per second after taking the private operator out of the picture.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: [pause] I keep wondering what that change feels like for the families who used to wait on the trucks.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Todos Santos–El Pescadero sits on the Pacific spine, lifestyle migration still arriving, yet the aquifer already runs in deficit.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The desert teaches you to notice every drop. How do the creative growers and the new residents share that same thin supply?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: After the October rains, Meganoticias says crews pulled eighteen tonnes of waste and 350 tyres off El Médano beach alone.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Altered stream beds sent it all straight to the sea. What would you ask the engineers who watch those beds every storm?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: [chuckle] I would ask whether the new drainage money will follow the natural paths instead of fighting them.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: And in East Cape, with the decks still on the table from September, the question becomes how the corridor to La Paz holds its lower density while the water moves.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: D2 plant sits at 76.58% complete. The city is asking the federal side for another 2.1 billion pesos to push D1 further.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: [breath] One plant at a time, yet the reef and the aquifer keep their own clocks.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: What would you ask the people living between the two plants right now?

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: I would ask what the morning light looks like when the tap finally runs clear without the truck.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The water stories keep circling back to the same quiet lines under the streets.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Exactly. The paving in Loreto and La Paz both include new drinking-water networks and sewer lines being handed to the utilities.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Wait—Conagua also closed two sources in Cabo San Lucas that supplied about 120 litres per second.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: And the La Paz paving project alone costs 48 million pesos with all new lines included.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Those lines are the thread. Without them the desal plants and the treatment upgrades have nowhere to land.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Gringo Gazette reports 25 illegal connections found in Los Cabos this year alone, pulling more than 300 litres per second.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Do you think the theft bill will change much on the ground?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The knowledge graph shows the design veto is still there without reuse or new supply.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: And the bill now proposes up to ten years in prison for that kind of extraction.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Meanwhile the second desal plant in Cabo San Lucas sits at 75% and will add 250 litres per second once it finishes next year.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The paving in Miramar reached 45 percent with the water network nearly ready for tie-in.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: It feels like the whole state is stitching new threads at once.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: So the legal supply grows while the hidden theft keeps draining it at the same time.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The portal's earlier Foresight editions kept saying water, grid and places set the 2050 ceiling.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: And the numbers back that up. Los Cabos received just 2.02m pesos in state water works from 2021 to 2026.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: That is the lowest of any municipality, even though the corridor carries the heaviest tourism load.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: I keep thinking about residents waiting up to 40 days for water in some areas.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: And spending as much as 2,000 pesos every two weeks on trucks. [chuckle]

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The governor called the shortage extremely delicate and asked Conagua to hurry the wastewater projects.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Those projects are only 60% advanced and still tied up in lawsuits.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The second plant will bring total desal capacity to 655 litres per second.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Serving more than 200,000 people once it is done.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: So the hidden design is this: new pipes and desal capacity only matter if the old leaks and theft stop first.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: But here is the strange part. The same week they announce the prison bill, the portal notes Los Cabos is already chasing water theft while the Sea of Cortez forum talks about doubling the regional economy.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The two ambitions sit on the same aquifer.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Four key aquifers already in deficit, the knowledge graph says. Growth without new supply or reuse is simply blocked.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The thread runs from the illegal well to the paving contract to the desal plant to the 2050 map.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: And every time we follow one story it pulls the others into view.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Did you know 22 of 39 aquifers sit in deficit right now.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: That number feels heavy. What does it look like on the ground.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Think of one family’s backyard well in the middle of the dry season. The pump keeps running but the level drops a little every year until one morning the hose spits air.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Mm. And the whole region loses −105.1 cubic hectometers each year according to CONAGUA.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Exactly. CONAGUA’s 2023 numbers put the total shortfall at that figure across those 22 aquifers.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: I keep picturing the same well but multiplied across the peninsula. What happens when the hose runs dry for everyone at once.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: That question sits behind every growth plan.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The Sea of Cortez Forum last week heard a call for 3.5% annual growth for 20 years.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: At the same time the same room talked about the missing planning tools for water. Hans Herrmann called for a five state treaty.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The desert teaches you the cost of every extra drop before you spend it.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Last month Hurricane Polo showed what happens when the system is already stretched. The levee at Puerto San Carlos gave way and water service was knocked out across parts of Comondú and Mulegé.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: One storm, one breach, and the everyday supply disappears for days.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: CFE said power came back quickly but the water lines took longer.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: It always comes back to the same quiet limit. [chuckle]

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The same limit that makes every new hotel or road feel heavier than it looks on paper.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What would you ask the next person who draws up a 20 year plan.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: I would ask how the numbers change when the aquifer is already running on air.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Turn on the tap in Los Cabos and what do you actually touch?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The pipe, sure, but the whole chain behind it. [chuckle]

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Exactly. One ordinary faucet opens onto four key aquifers already in DMA deficit.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: So the water arrives only if someone already answered the viability questions first.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Those questions sit in the dq_viabilidad_proyecto package. Water has to clear DMA, aquifers, and desal before anything else moves.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Wait, so even a small housing project gets checked against all that before the first drawing gets approved? Really?

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Yes, and Los Cabos tourism sits at the center of the demand pressure along the whole corridor.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: And the people who keep that list straight meet in the mesas de trabajo.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The notes from 30 sep 2026 show how the water mesa tracks every proposal against the four aquifers in deficit.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The water mesa belongs to CEA and CONAGUA.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: They sit with the other tables, the ones on energy, urban plans, and conservation, all checking the same project.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: So the faucet is really a committee decision made visible.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: And the asset managers keep the pipes alive under ISO 55000 rules from the Institute of Asset Management in 2014.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: And still no parque industrial has both a site and a water allocation listed anywhere in the records.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Mm. Every valve, every pump, tracked like a living thing across decades. [pause]

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: I keep thinking about the coastal stretch and what rising seas might do to those same pipes.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The IPCC SROCC lays out the exposure clearly for places like this.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: IRENA data shows solar can make desal cheap enough to add supply without breaking the aquifers further, especially with BCS top-tier solar resource.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Along the CSL to SJD corridor the tourism demand shapes everything else that follows.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: But only if the mesas already agreed the desal plant fits the POERBCS and PDU.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: One glass of water therefore carries the weight of every rule that said yes.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: I wonder what the next round of mesas will unlock for the coastal pipes. [laugh]

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: And the ones that still say not yet. [pause]

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The hidden design is just that long quiet conversation before the tap ever runs. [breath]

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The portal’s vision for water toward 2050 starts with the ceiling that limits everything else.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: 22 of 39 aquifers sit in deficit, according to CONAGUA in 2023.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: That total shortfall of 105.1 cubic hectometers per year feels like a hard line.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: 25 illegal taps in Los Cabos alone, pulling more than 300 liters per second.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: And only three in ten residents enjoy constant supply, per the ENCIG 2025 data.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The aspiration is simple: new growth that does not lean on those same stressed aquifers.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Continuous supply stops being the rare case, and reuse actually adds to the margin.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The portal offers no single 2050 equilibrium number, just that direction.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: One lever already moving is the second Cabo San Lucas desal plant.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: 75% complete, adding 250 liters per second, for a combined 655 liters per second by 2027.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: It is a supply tool under construction, not permission to keep draining the deficit aquifers.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Closing those illegal connections would recover volume that never reaches users now.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Growth permits would then tie directly to mean annual availability under NOM-011, without pretending credit against the shortfall.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The demand-supply board keeps any local deficit from being masked by headroom elsewhere on paper.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The tendencia reading stays polycentric rather than one coastal formula repeated north to south.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Los Cabos carries the tourism engine under water and power stress, while Comondú holds more room as an agricultural hub.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: East Cape stays in tension with protected areas, and Loreto anchors tourism with conservation.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Each place keeps its distinct role instead of becoming a diluted version of Cabo statewide.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: New projects only go where water and energy show real margin or a non-DMA source like desal.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: East Cape and Loreto would need to respect ANP and POEL ceilings before any hospitality expansion.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Comondú and the north could add production and energy, yet without emptying services or protected zones elsewhere.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: On the watchlist, the second desal plant progress, the Los Cabos POEL 2026 water obligations, and federal action on theft.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: A federal bill now carries penalties up to ten years in prison for water theft.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: That pairs with ongoing closures of illegal connections in Los Cabos.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Housing for Wellbeing plots would also need checking against actual water and service capacity.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The question is whether those separate vocations can hold without one place emptying another.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Mm. That is what the board is meant to test.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: I keep coming back to one thought about water here. It feels like the whole peninsula is teaching us something quiet about limits and flow, like the slow pulse under everything.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Which one?

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: How the desert and the sea keep the same slow conversation going, only in different tones. The waves come in, the arroyos wait for rain, and somehow that balance holds the light.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: [pause] And we stand right in the middle of it, trying not to interrupt.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Exactly. It makes me wonder what happens when we stop rushing to answer and just watch how the place already moves.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Really? You mean just letting the place speak first before we decide what it needs?

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Yes. The real work is learning how to listen before we speak, the way the dunes seem to listen to the wind.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: [chuckle] That feels true. Like waiting for the right set before you drop in, feeling the swell rather than chasing it.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: [breath] The feeling that stays with me is that patience might be the quietest kind of design, the one the desert has been practicing for centuries.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Yes. And maybe that is the one thing we can carry forward, this sense of waiting with the land instead of against it.
